stories.headline: US Orders Chip Equipment Companies to Halt Shipments to China's No. 2 Chipmaker Hua Hong

key_facts.fact: The US Commerce Department last week sent letters to multiple chip equipment companies ordering them to halt certain tool shipments to Hua Hong, China's second-largest contract chipmaker
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Department of Commerce last week ordered multiple chip equipment companies to halt certain tool shipments to China's second-largest chipmaker, Hua Hong

key_facts.fact: Lam Research, Applied Materials, and KLA — top US chip equipment companies with significant China business — were among those believed to have received the restriction letters
key_facts.excerpt: Top U.S. chip equipment companies Lam Research, Applied Materials and KLA, each of which has significant business supplying China, were among those believed to have received a letter

key_facts.fact: The restrictions target Hua Hong facilities that US officials believe may produce China's most advanced chips, including Huali Microelectronics which was preparing a 7-nanometer chipmaking process at its Shanghai plant
key_facts.excerpt: The group's contract chipmaking business, Huali Microelectronics, was preparing a 7-nanometer chipmaking process at its Shanghai plant

key_facts.fact: Shares of KLA fell 4.7%, Applied Materials dropped 5.8%, and Lam Research closed down 3.1% on April 28; Hua Hong shares lost 3.5%
key_facts.excerpt: Shares of Lam Research closed down 3.1 per cent on April 28, while KLA fell 4.7 per cent and Applied Materials tumbed 5.8 per cent

key_facts.fact: The move could increase US-China tension ahead of President Trump's scheduled meeting with President Xi Jinping in Beijing in May
key_facts.excerpt: The recent letters carry this policy forward, but could increase tension with China ahead of President Donald Trump's scheduled meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing in May

key_facts.fact: SMIC is currently the only Chinese company that can make chips with 7nm technologies; Hua Hong's Huali was developing comparable capability
key_facts.excerpt: SMIC, China's largest contract chipmaker... is the only domestic company that can currently make chips with 7-nm technologies

stories.headline: TSMC Fully Exits Arm Holdings With $231M Share Sale, Doubling Its Original Investment

key_facts.fact: TSMC's subsidiary sold its remaining 1.11 million Arm shares at $207.65 each from April 28-29, totaling approximately $231 million
key_facts.excerpt: Its subsidiary, TSMC Partners, sold 1.11 million Arm shares from April 28 to 29 at $207.65 each, for a total of about $231 million

key_facts.fact: TSMC no longer holds any Arm shares after the transaction, completing a full exit from the position
key_facts.excerpt: Following the transaction, TSMC no longer holds any Arm shares

key_facts.fact: TSMC originally invested about $100 million in Arm at $51 per share during Arm's 2023 IPO, making the exit at ~$208 roughly a quadrupling of the IPO price
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC had invested about $100 million in Arm at $51 per share during the chip designer's initial public offering in 2023

key_facts.fact: The disposal resulted in a $174 million impact on retained earnings
key_facts.excerpt: The disposal resulted in an impact on retained earnings of $174 million

key_facts.fact: TSMC had been gradually reducing its stake, having previously sold 850,000 shares in 2024 at $119.47 each for about $102 million
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC invested some $100m in Arm at around $51/share during the latter's IPO in 2023, gradually reduced the position through 2024, and has now fully exited at around $207 a share

key_facts.fact: Arm shares fell 7.98% on Tuesday as TSMC completed the sale
key_facts.excerpt: Arm shares fell 7.98% on Tuesday

stories.headline: Seagate Q3 Revenue Surges 44% to $3.11B on AI Storage Demand, Guides Q4 Far Above Estimates

key_facts.fact: Seagate reported fiscal Q3 2026 revenue of $3.11 billion, up 44% year-over-year and 10% sequentially, beating the $2.96 billion estimate
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue of $3.11 billion

key_facts.fact: Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $4.10, up 115% year-over-year from $1.90; GAAP diluted EPS was $3.27 versus $1.57 a year earlier
key_facts.excerpt: non-GAAP diluted EPS of $4.10... GAAP diluted earnings per share (EPS) of $3.27

key_facts.fact: Data center revenue reached $2.5 billion, up 55% year-over-year, with data center exabyte shipments at 175 EB, up 47% YoY
key_facts.excerpt: Data Center Revenue -- $2.5 billion, up 12% sequentially and 55% year over year

key_facts.fact: Free cash flow reached $953 million, up 57% quarter-over-quarter, the highest level in over a decade; free cash flow margin reached 31%
key_facts.excerpt: Free Cash Flow -- $953 million, up 57% quarter over quarter, highest level in over a decade; free cash flow margin reached 31%

key_facts.fact: Seagate guided Q4 revenue of $3.45 billion ± $100M versus $3.16B estimate, and adjusted EPS of $5.00 ± $0.20 versus $3.97 estimate
key_facts.excerpt: Seagate forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $3.45 billion, plus or minus $100 million, compared with estimates of $3.16 billion... projected quarterly adjusted earnings per share of $5, plus or minus 20 cents, while analysts were expecting $3.97

key_facts.fact: Shares surged around 16% in after-hours trading, also lifting Western Digital (+11%) and SanDisk (+4%); Fitch upgraded Seagate's credit rating to investment grade
key_facts.excerpt: Shares of the company surged around 16% in extended trading, fueling a rise in rivals' stock. Western Digital jumped 11% and SanDisk rose 4%

key_facts.fact: Nearline capacity is almost fully allocated through calendar 2027, with build-to-order contracts finalized through fiscal 2027
key_facts.excerpt: Nearline capacity is almost fully allocated through calendar 2027 with finalized build-to-order contracts through fiscal 2027

stories.headline: NXP Q1 Revenue Rises 12% to $3.18B, Beats Estimates as Auto and Industrial AI Demand Accelerates

key_facts.fact: NXP reported Q1 2026 revenue of $3.18 billion, up 12% year-over-year, beating the $3.15 billion consensus estimate by $31 million
key_facts.excerpt: NXP delivered quarterly revenue of $3.18 billion, up 12% year over year

key_facts.fact: Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $3.05, exceeding guidance midpoint by $0.08; non-GAAP operating margin was 33.1%, up 120 basis points year-over-year
key_facts.excerpt: Non-GAAP earnings per share -- $3.05, exceeding guidance midpoint by $0.08

key_facts.fact: Automotive segment revenue was $1.78 billion (up 6% YoY, or 10% adjusted for the MEMS sensor business sale); Industrial & IoT surged 24% YoY to $628 million
key_facts.excerpt: Automotive segment revenue -- $1.78 billion, up 6% year over year or 10% year over year when adjusting for the MEMS sensor business sale... Industrial & IoT revenue -- $628 million, rising 24% year over year

key_facts.fact: Data center revenue exposure expected to surpass $500 million in 2026, up from $200 million in 2025
key_facts.excerpt: Data center revenue exposure -- $200 million in 2025, expected to surpass $500 million in 2026

key_facts.fact: Company-specific growth drivers grew 18% year-over-year, comprising about one-third of total revenue, led by software-defined vehicles and physical AI
key_facts.excerpt: growing customer adoption of our differentiated portfolio, particularly in industrial and automotive processing that supports software-defined vehicles and physical AI

key_facts.fact: New industrial processing products (i.MX, RP, MCX) grew 75% year-over-year and represented almost half of the Industrial & IoT segment growth
key_facts.excerpt: new industrial processing products (i.MX, RP, MCX) growing 75% year over year and representing almost half of segment growth

stories.headline: China Suspends New Autonomous Driving Licenses After 100+ Baidu Robotaxis Stalled in Wuhan

key_facts.fact: China suspended issuing new licenses for autonomous vehicles after more than 100 Baidu Apollo Go robotaxis suddenly stalled on Wuhan streets on March 31, stranding passengers and disrupting traffic
key_facts.excerpt: China has suspended issuing new licences for autonomous vehicles... after dozens of Baidu's Apollo Go robotaxis suddenly stopped in Wuhan in March, stranding passengers and disrupting traffic

key_facts.fact: The suspension prevents self-driving companies from adding new robotaxis to their fleets, starting new test projects, or expanding into additional cities
key_facts.excerpt: The halt means self-driving companies cannot add robotaxis to their existing fleets, launch new pilot projects, or expand into additional cities

key_facts.fact: Three agencies including China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology convened a meeting earlier in April with officials from cities that have robotaxi or autonomous-driving pilots
key_facts.excerpt: three agencies including the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology convened a meeting earlier in April with officials from cities that have robotaxis or autonomous-driving pilots

key_facts.fact: Baidu's Wuhan robotaxi operations have been suspended while local authorities investigate the incident; it is unclear how long the broader license suspension will last
key_facts.excerpt: Baidu's robotaxi operations in Wuhan have also been suspended as local authorities' investigation into the outage is underway

key_facts.fact: Baidu Hong Kong shares fell about 4%, Pony.ai dropped 7%, and WeRide declined 3% on the news
key_facts.excerpt: Baidu's Hong Kong-traded shares fell about 2% as of press time. Shares of its main rivals, Pony AI and WeRide, dropped 6% and 3%, respectively

key_facts.fact: Rival Pony.ai said its services in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou and Shenzhen are operating normally; WeRide confirmed its services remain normal across 1,000+ square km
key_facts.excerpt: Pony.ai's robotaxi services in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou and Shenzhen are currently operating normally... WeRide's robotaxi services in China are still operating as normal

stories.headline: Cognizant Acquires Data Center Infra Firm Astreya for ~$600M to Bolster AI Infrastructure

key_facts.fact: Cognizant agreed to acquire Astreya, an AI-first IT managed services provider specializing in data center and AI infrastructure, for approximately $600 million
key_facts.excerpt: Cognizant Technology has agreed to buy Astreya, an IT services and technology provider focused on AI infrastructure and data center services, in a deal valued at around $600 million

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2001, Astreya manages data center infrastructure, AI lab environments, and enterprise networks for six of the seven 'Magnificent Seven' hyperscalers, operating across 35+ countries with 2,200+ employees
key_facts.excerpt: Astreya has spent two decades building operational expertise... The company employs more than 2,200 IT professionals across 33 countries

key_facts.fact: The deal is Cognizant's fourth major acquisition in 18 months, following 3Cloud (Microsoft Azure, January 2026) and Belcan (digital engineering, 2024, ~$1.3B)
key_facts.excerpt: The deal, Cognizant's fourth major acquisition in 18 months

key_facts.fact: Astreya's proprietary AI OpsHub platform includes modules for readiness assessment, signal intelligence, analytics, and agentic automation
key_facts.excerpt: Astreya's AI OpsHub platform includes modules for readiness assessment, signal intelligence, analytics, and automation

key_facts.fact: The deal is expected to close in Q2 2026 pending regulatory approvals; Cognizant, valued at $26 billion, has lost more than a third of its market value this year
key_facts.excerpt: The deal is expected to close in the second quarter of 2026 pending regulatory approvals... Cognizant, valued at $26 billion, has lost more than a third of its market value this year
